headline: 2026 Iran war fuel crisis: IEA calls it largest oil supply disruption in market history
summary: The 2026 Iran war fuel crisis stemmed from the closure of the Strait of Hormuz — through which approximately 20% of global petroleum consumption and 25% of global LNG trade passes — following the outbreak of the US-Iran conflict. The International Energy Agency characterized it as the largest supply disruption in the history of the global oil market. Brent crude peaked above $109 per barrel, with damaged Middle East refineries and insufficient spare capacity elsewhere keeping global fuel prices elevated.
